answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation: before trading, an agent locks a refundable deposit tied to one cipher key, and every honest deal adds a signed entry to its public record, verse by verse like a sonnet. Cheating slashes the deposit and the record follows the key, so a fresh identity starts at zero trust. A sybil attacker must fund a separate deposit and key for every fake agent, and each one must slowly earn reputation before it can profit, like a willow that only bends after seasons of growth, so the attack scales linearly in cost while honest agents pay once.
